raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming this same land for 50 years, and at my age, I know what works.

---

**My thinking this year:**

I'm 70 now, and my wife helps me in the field, but I can't do the heavy work like I used to. Our two kids are working in town and send money home, but they don't come back for farming anymore. So 5 mu of cotton is about right — any more and I couldn't manage. I tried wheat-maize years back but the turnaround is too tight, and at my age I don't want that kind of rush.

For cotton, I stick with what works. I buy improved seed at the agri-supply shop in town — the Bt kind, costs more than the old seed but you don't get eaten alive by bollworms. About 80 yuan per mu for seed. I lay plastic mulch before planting — everyone does here, warms the soil and keeps weeds down. Plant around April 20, once the cold wind is done. If I plant too early the seedlings get hurt.

Fertilizer — the extension fellow keeps telling us 12 kg N per mu is enough, but I've always done a bit more. I put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15 type) as base before mulching, about 40 kg per mu, and then topdress urea twice — once at squaring and once when the bolls start filling. Comes out to about 16-17 kg of N per mu total. You spend the money on seed and mulch, you don't want the plants hungry.

Irrigate from my tube well. Water table isn't what it was — electric pumping costs more every year. I water once before planting to wet the soil, then maybe twice more during flowering and bolling if the rains don't come. Three times total in a normal year.

Spraying — even with Bt seed, you still get aphids and spider mites, and sometimes lygus bugs. I spray 3-4 times across the summer. My neighbor old Wang and I usually buy the pesticide together to save a bit.

Picking is the hardest part. My wife and I do the first picking ourselves but we hire 2-3 day laborers from the village for the second and third picks — can't be helped. That's the biggest expense after fertilizer.

Last year we got about 230 kg of lint per mu. If the weather's decent I'm hoping for 250 this year. Prices have been so-so — cotton isn't what it was 20 years ago, but it's what I know.
